definition: TLS is a protocol that authenticates the other party, usually the server, and encrypts the bytes of a connection. A handshake agrees on keys and checks a certificate; application data sent afterward is protected. HTTPS is HTTP running over TLS.
details: The certificate tells the client which name the server claims. The client trusts it only if a certificate it already trusts signed that claim, directly or through a chain.
examples: A mail submission connection protected the same way
